notes.title: 日本人! We need your help!
notes.content:
Hi フォックスライダー, 

Once again we are working on a [b]Japanese version[/b] of our coming title [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1288410/outshine/]Outshine[/url]. 

Just like Epistory and Nanotale, Outshine will work with companion words which are romanized versions of the words you have to type in Japanese. 

Thanks to you we learned a bit more about Japanese localization while developing our typing game and now we understand that there are different ways to romanize it. There is the Hepburn romanization that generally follows English phonology with Romance vowels. But also the Nihon-shiki romanization originally invented for Japanese and his modified variant the Kunrei-shiki. 

[h3]So our question is: What romanization Japanese would prefer in Outshine?
[/h3]
Please, if you are a [b]player from Japan[/b], vote using that [url=https://forms.gle/qCtGH2ZpogucoX5J9]google form[/url].

notes.title: Announcement: Release and next updates
notes.content:
Hi Fox Riders, 

I hope that you are all doing well wherever you are in this world. 

The COVID-19 situation affected us all personally in different ways, but it also affected the video game industry. On our side, we worked hard on Nanotale to meet our release deadline that was planned for the end October 2020. This is still something that we could reach but without the polish and testing that would require the game to be perfect. For these reasons, we decided to delay the release to early 2021. 

The good news is that, meanwhile, we secured a deal with STADIA allowing us to keep some cool features that we were sad to drop earlier. Thanks to that, we’ll be able to rework some parts of the game that were confusing or seemed unfinished from your feedback. 


[h2]NEXT UPDATES[/h2]

That said, it doesn’t mean that we won’t release anything until the final release. Of course, we will continue to update the game with some rework on the areas and the story of the game to make it a better experience. We also plan to add the voice over, so you will enjoy a more immersive game experience.


[h2]CLOSED BETA[/h2]

Moreover, we plan to do a closed beta of the final biome of Nanotale allowing some of you to reach the end of the game before the final release. We can’t say when yet, but we’ll let you know as soon as we can on our [url=http://www.discord.gg/fishingcactus]Discord server[/url].

For that reason, we highly recommend you to start a fresh game before playing the new update in order to avoid any conflict with the new part of the story. The game supports multiple save points.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33924863/4fdaeaf29aaf0a396e35fc46f10ba2605ca3c252.jpg[/img]

[h1]Cellular automaton[/h1]

[i]Cellu-what?[/i]
It’s a way of simulating a world using a divide and conquer strategy. Instead of having a massive “World Simulator™” it’s often easier to simulate each object when making a game, This strategy goes further by dividing the world into uniform cells. Each cell has a state and a set of rules to change, if possible, into another state. Cellular automata are used in a very wide range of scientific domains, including computer science, mathematics, physics, and many others. The most famous is probably [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conway's_Game_of_Life]Conway's Game of Life[/url], it has only four rules and two states and you can already see a lot of patterns emerging from its simple concept.

If you want to read more about it and about how we use it in Nanotale, there's an artcile written by our programmer on [url=https://www.indiedb.com/games/nanotale-typing-chronicles/news/using-a-cellular-automaton-in-video-games]Indie DB[/url].

[i]Something is wrong with the heart of magic. Play a young archivist venturing out into a dying world, cataloging its mysteries and its wonders to unearth the truth.[/i]
